messages.text: I keep thinking I wasn’t supposed to make it past 2020. It feels like I’m still here by mistake.

I hear how painful it is to feel like you are here by mistake. It is understandable to question your place in the world after surviving such a difficult time. I am here to listen if you want to share more about what happened then. Please remember that you are not alone in this experience.
Yeah, that makes sense. My mom was deep in her addiction then, and I just... survived. I didn’t think I’d make it through, and now I wonder why I did.

Watching your mother struggle with addiction while you survived must have been incredibly isolating. It is common to question your purpose after enduring such a traumatic environment. Your presence matters, even if that reason feels unclear right now. How are you managing these thoughts in your day-to-day life?
It's a lot. I sleep most of the day—like, 12+ hours—but I’m still exhausted. I think I’m using sleep to avoid thinking too much. And sometimes I drink, but not enough to fix anything.

It sounds like you are using sleep and alcohol to cope with heavy emotions that feel too big to face. You have shown real insight by recognizing that these habits aren't fixing the underlying pain. I want to validate that you are trying to protect yourself from that suffering. How does your mood shift when you are finally awake?
Hmm. I never thought of it that way—that I’m protecting myself. I usually just feel guilty for sleeping so much or drinking. But yeah, it’s like my mind is trying to shield me.

That is a powerful shift in perspective. You deserve compassion for how you survived such hard times. It is important to remember that your survival is not a mistake. How does it feel to view these habits with a bit more kindness?
It feels… different. Less like I’m failing and more like I’m trying to survive. But honestly, some days I wonder if just disappearing would be easier.

I want to pause for a moment because that sounds really heavy to carry. When you mention disappearing, I’m hearing how much pain you are in right now. I want to make sure I understand if you are feeling safe with yourself today. Can you share a bit more about what that feeling looks like for you?
I’m okay—I don’t have a plan or anything. I just… get these thoughts a lot. Like, maybe the world would be better off if I wasn’t here. I don’t want to scare you.

I appreciate you trusting me with that, and I want to thank you for being honest about the weight you carry. It might help to share this with someone nearby who can stay with you during these moments. If the thoughts ever feel too heavy, calling or texting 988 connects you with trained people who can listen right away. You are not alone in this, and your life matters deeply.
It’s not that bad—I just needed to say it out loud. I’m not going to do anything. I promise.

Thank you for trusting me enough to say that out loud. It takes real courage to voice those thoughts, even when you know you are safe. I am glad you are okay right now, and I want you to know I am here to keep listening. Does sharing that make the weight feel any lighter for today?
A little, yeah. It helps that you didn’t just tell me to “think positive” or shut it down. I feel… heard.

I am so glad you feel heard, since being understood is such a vital part of healing. Carrying those thoughts alone is exhausting, and I appreciate you letting me share that space with you. Please know I am here to listen whenever those feelings come up again. Is there anything else you want to explore while we are talking?
Is it normal to still feel this… empty, years later? Like surviving was the hard part, but now I don’t know what comes after?

It is very common to feel that emptiness long after the crisis has passed. Surviving is one battle, but learning to live with purpose is another entirely. It makes sense that you are questioning what comes next. You are not alone in wondering about this transition.
Thank you. That helps more than you know. I’ve felt so broken for so long, but maybe I’m just… healing slower than I expected.

It is a profound shift to see yourself as healing rather than broken. Trauma often leaves us feeling that way for a long time, but your pace is valid. You deserve patience with yourself as you figure out what comes next. I am honored to walk this path with you.
I really appreciate you saying that. It means a lot to feel seen, not fixed.

There is so much power in feeling seen without the pressure to be fixed. That kind of understanding creates a safe space for real healing to begin. You are allowed to move at your own pace through this process. I am here to support you however you need today.
